learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected four water molecules and locked it in.
observations.exploration: One set changed six H2/four O2 to four H2/three O2/two water. Until exhausted produced zero H2/one O2/six water. Added one H2: still disabled reaction. Added second H2: enabled; reacted to eight water and zero remaining reactants. Start over restored original six/four, then exhausted to original six-water result.
observations.reveal: Corrected to six, explained two-to-one recipe means six H2 need three O2 and H2 limits despite larger initial count. Emphasized matching recipe ratio rather than choosing smaller pile.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Separate labeled molecular rows, reaction equation, leftover oxygen pair and six water clusters visible. Disabled reaction controls and no-full-set message agreed with counts. Reveal readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete recipe and counts support a meaningful limiting-resource commitment.
prediction.evidence: Four, six and eight yield alternatives.

interaction.reason: Single sets, exhaustion, adding one versus two molecules and reset test complete-set boundary.
interaction.evidence: One extra H2 insufficient; second unlocks two more water.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains ratio-limited yield using observed leftovers.
payoff.evidence: Six H2 need three O2 with four available.

clarity.reason: Molecule drawings and recipe ratio align with counter changes.
clarity.evidence: Two H2 plus one O2 makes two water.

transfer.reason: General recipe principle stated without a concrete new application.

accessibility.evidence: Text molecule counts and disabled states available; screen reader, keyboard, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: More numerous starting reactant runs out first.
surprise.evidence: Hydrogen six versus oxygen four, but hydrogen exhausted.

visualExplanation.reason: Leftover rows and product clusters make the ratio visible.
visualExplanation.evidence: One oxygen pair remains beside six water.

playfulness.reason: React, add and restart controls support boundary experimentation.

practicalValue.reason: Explains limiting reagents through recipe matching.

depth.reason: Links stoichiometry and discrete complete sets.
depth.evidence: Odd extra molecule cannot form a full set.

complexity.reason: Simple counts support unfamiliar chemical symbols and stoichiometric ratio.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Normalize available molecules by recipe coefficients rather than raw pile size.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Five clear buttons with contextual disabled states.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Chemical molecule notation and reaction sets.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Subscripts, reaction arrow and two-to-one ratio.

whyCool: The smaller pile can have leftovers when the recipe consumes the larger pile faster.
caveat: This is a discrete recipe model; no alternate reaction or fresh limiting-resource application was tested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
